last_transition_reason: The proof establishes both directions of the equivalence using standard floor-function inequalities and the assumption 0 <= t < 1. It matches the lemma statement exactly, with no semantic drift and no dependency issues.
latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n > 1 and a real number t with 0 <= t < 1.

We prove the equivalence in both directions.

First, assume floor(n t) = n - 1. Since floor(n t) is the greatest integer less than or equal to n t, the inequality floor(n t) <= n t gives n - 1 <= n t. Dividing by the positive integer n yields t >= (n - 1)/n. Together with the given assumption t < 1, this gives (n - 1)/n <= t < 1.

Conversely, assume (n - 1)/n <= t < 1. Multiplying by the positive integer n gives n - 1 <= n t < n. Because n - 1 is an integer and n t is strictly less than n, the floor of n t must be n - 1. Hence floor(n t) = n - 1.

Therefore, for every integer n > 1 and every real t with 0 <= t < 1, floor(n t) = n - 1 if and only if (n - 1)/n <= t < 1.
